Manage webhooks

Source: R/webhooks.R
grist_webhooks.Rd

Webhooks make Grist send an HTTP POST to a URL when records in a table change.

  • grist_webhooks() lists a document's webhooks with their delivery status.

  • grist_webhook_create() creates a webhook.

  • grist_webhook_update() changes a webhook.

  • grist_webhook_delete() deletes a webhook permanently.

  • grist_webhook_queue_clear() discards undelivered payloads, for one webhook or for the whole document. Use it when the queue has built up because an endpoint was unreachable.

Usage

grist_webhooks(doc)

grist_webhook_create(
  doc,
  url,
  table,
  event_types = c("add", "update"),
  name = NULL,
  memo = NULL,
  enabled = TRUE,
  is_ready_column = NULL
)

grist_webhook_update(
  doc,
  id,
  url = NULL,
  table = NULL,
  event_types = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  memo = NULL,
  enabled = NULL,
  is_ready_column = NULL
)

grist_webhook_delete(doc, id, ask = NULL)

grist_webhook_queue_clear(doc, id = NULL)

Arguments

doc

A grist_doc object, document ID or document URL. See grist_doc().

url

URL that receives the POST requests.

table

Table ID, as listed by grist_tables().

event_types

Events that trigger the webhook: "add", "update" or both.

name, memo

Optional name and description. For grist_webhook_update(), NULL leaves the value unchanged and NA clears it.

enabled

Whether the webhook is active.

is_ready_column

Optional ID of a boolean column. When set, an event is only sent once the column is TRUE. For grist_webhook_update(), NA clears it.

id

A webhook ID, as returned by grist_webhook_create() or listed by grist_webhooks(). For grist_webhook_queue_clear(), NULL clears the queues of all webhooks in the document.

ask

Whether to prompt before running. NULL (the default) and TRUE prompt in an interactive session and error in a script. FALSE skips the prompt.

Value

grist_webhooks() returns a data frame with one row per webhook: id, name, memo, url, enabled, table, event_types (a list-column), is_ready_column, and delivery columns num_waiting, status, last_success_time and last_failure_time (POSIXct in UTC), last_error_message and last_http_status. The webhook's unsubscribe key is not included. grist_webhook_create() returns the new webhook ID, and the other functions return doc, all invisibly.

Deleting

grist_webhook_delete() asks for confirmation in an interactive session and refuses to run in a script unless ask = FALSE, like grist_doc_delete().

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc("am2iHJ9Amvo7Ve3EE5emtu")

id <- grist_webhook_create(
  doc,
  url = "https://example.com/hook",
  table = "Projects",
  name = "new-project"
)
grist_webhooks(doc)

grist_webhook_update(doc, id, enabled = FALSE, memo = NA)
grist_webhook_queue_clear(doc, id)
grist_webhook_delete(doc, id)
}
